pages.title: Upload a T12
pages.description: Give a property its T12, so the app can read it and start the underwriting.
pages.intro: The T12 is where a property’s underwriting starts: every account, month by month, and the in-place NOI. Upload it in Underwriting: the app saves it in the property’s folder, reads and checks it, and starts the underwriting draft from it. Without a T12 there is no underwriting, and no refinance.
before: The property in the app — see [Add a property](add-a-property).
The property’s T12 as an Excel or CSV export.

steps.text: Click **+** at the end of the tab strip, then **Underwriting & Sizing**. Underwriting opens in a tab of its own.

marks.text: Opens the menu of tools that open in a tab.

marks.label: Underwriting & Sizing
marks.text: Opens the Underwriting tab.

steps.text: Pick the property in **Property**. A property that already has a T12 loads it, with its underwriting.

marks.label: Property
marks.text: The property the T12 belongs to.

marks.label: The T12 box
marks.text: Drop the file here.

marks.label: choose a file
marks.text: Or pick the file in your computer’s file window.

steps.text: Drag the T12 file from its folder and let go over the box. Or click **choose a file**, pick the T12 and click **Open**.
Wait while the file is read. The app’s own reader and Claude each read it. When every check passes and both agree, the T12 is used at once, and the underwriting draft starts from it.

marks.label: Checked by the reader and the AI
marks.text: Both readings agree: the figures are in use.

marks.label: NOI used
marks.text: The in-place NOI from this T12, and the months it covers.

marks.label: Review the reading
marks.text: How each row of the file was read.

callouts.text: When a check fails, Claude reads the file differently, or Claude isn’t connected, a window asks you to decide. Until then the T12 waits, unused. See [Check a T12](check-a-t12).

steps.text: Type the number of apartments in **Units**. When the app asks to update the property’s profile to match, click **OK**.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: From the rent roll. Sets the replacement reserves and every per-unit figure.

marks.label: Gross potential rent — per year
marks.text: Optional: a year’s rent with every unit leased at market.

marks.label: Average rent per unit — per month
marks.text: Or the average monthly rent for one unit.

callouts.text: A gross potential rent above the T12’s comes into the draft as a suggestion, never by itself. Leave it blank to keep the statement’s rent.

next.text: Draft Safe and Aggressive from the T12.
See how each row of a T12 was read, and correct it.
Every part of the Underwriting tab, named.

pages.title: Draft the underwriting
pages.description: Turn the T12 into a Safe and an Aggressive underwriting, with a story for every change.
pages.intro: The underwriting is the NOI you ask a lender to accept: the T12, with the changes you can explain. It has two versions. Safe is what you would defend line by line; Aggressive is Safe plus the changes a cautious lender may not accept. Both start as the T12 less the replacement reserves, and stay a draft until you approve them.
before: A T12 for the property — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: Scroll down to **Underwriting assumptions**, under the underwriting table.
Type the property’s **Vacancy**, **Management fee** and **Reserves / unit**, and your payroll and R&M benchmarks.

marks.label: Vacancy
marks.text: A vacancy that runs above it gets a suggestion at it.

marks.label: Management fee
marks.text: The same, as a % of effective gross income.

marks.label: Reserves / unit
marks.text: A year’s replacement reserves per unit, taken off Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Save to property record
marks.text: Keeps them with the property, for every screen.

steps.text: Click **Save to property record**.

callouts.text: The assumptions never change the underwriting by themselves. A line that runs worse than one gets a suggestion in the draft; one that would lower the NOI gets only a warning.

steps.text: Scroll back up to the three figures under the T12: the in-place NOI, and the Safe and Aggressive underwriting NOI after the reserves.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The T12’s own NOI.

marks.label: Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: The T12 with Safe’s changes, less the reserves.

marks.label: Aggressive underwriting NOI
marks.text: Safe plus Aggressive’s own changes, less the reserves.

marks.label: draft · not approved yet
marks.text: Nothing else uses it until you approve it.

steps.text: In the underwriting bar above the table, click **Safe** or **Aggressive**. The **Underwriting** column shows that version.

marks.label: Safe
marks.text: Shows the Safe version.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Shows the Aggressive version.

marks.label: The two NOIs
marks.text: The version shown first, then the other.

steps.text: Click a figure in the **Underwriting** column. A window opens with every account of that line: change them there, one by one, each with its story. See [Change an account](change-an-account).

marks.label: Underwriting · Safe
marks.text: The version the switch shows, line by line.

marks.label: A figure
marks.text: Click it to open the line’s accounts.

callouts.text: Aggressive starts as Safe and adds its own changes; on an account changed for both, Aggressive’s own change wins in Aggressive. Every change says where it applies: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

Money the T12 has no account for goes in with **+ Add an account** — see [Add an account](add-an-account). For the changes Claude finds for you, see [Use Claude’s stories and suggestions](use-claudes-stories).

steps.text: Scroll below the table. One box per version adds it up: the T12 NOI, each change grouped by its kind with its story, the replacement reserves and the underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Safe — how it adds up
marks.text: T12 NOI + each change − reserves.

marks.label: reconciles to the dollar
marks.text: The changes add up exactly.

marks.label: = Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: The figure you approve.

steps.text: When both versions are what you would show, approve them — see [Approve the underwriting](approve-the-underwriting). Until then nothing else uses the draft: **What to push**, at the bottom of the tab, waits for the approval.

marks.label: Approve the underwriting first
marks.text: What to push works from the approved Safe and Aggressive.

next.text: Change an account, with its kind and story.
Let Claude find the changes a lender would accept.
Make Safe and Aggressive the property’s underwriting.

pages.title: Change an account
pages.description: Give one account a new figure in the underwriting, with its kind and the story the lender reads.
pages.intro: Every change in the underwriting is made on one account, with its kind (why it changes), the versions it applies to, and a story. Before you save, a preview shows the account’s 12 months before and after, the line and the NOI. Here, a heavy winter’s snow removal is brought to a normal year.
before: A T12 for the property — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: In the **Underwriting** column, click the figure of the account’s line. The pro forma window opens with every account of the line — a $0 one too — and its 12 months as the statement shows them.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: In the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive.

marks.label: An account
marks.text: Click it to change it.

steps.text: Click the account. The ways to change it open under it.

marks.label: New amount
marks.text: A new yearly figure; 0 takes the account out.

marks.label: Spread over years
marks.text: For a cost paid once every few years.

marks.label: Annualize
marks.text: Its last 3, 6 or 12 months, made a year.

marks.label: % of revenue
marks.text: A share of revenue.

marks.label: Per unit
marks.text: Dollars per apartment a year.

callouts.text: These steps use **New amount**. For the other ways, see [The pro forma window](ref-pro-forma#ways-to-change-an-account).

steps.text: Click **New amount** and type the account’s yearly figure.
Pick the **Kind**: why it changes. Here **Normalized**, an unusual year brought to a normal one.
Under **Apply to**, click **Safe**, **Aggressive** or **Both**.
Write the **Story**: the reason the lender reads. To start from a draft, click **Draft it with Claude**.

marks.label: Its new amount
marks.text: The account’s yearly figure.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Why it changes.

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: Required.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: The account’s 12 months in the T12 and after the change.

steps.text: Check the preview, then click **Save the change**. The window stays open on the line: the account shows its new figure, and a tag says where it applies and its kind.

marks.label: The changed account
marks.text: Now 9,000 in Safe and in Aggressive.

marks.label: The tag
marks.text: Where it applies and its kind. Hover it to read the story.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: The line’s totals follow.

callouts.text: One cause often moves several accounts. Pick a story you already wrote in **Same story as…** and it fills in; then adjust it.

steps.text: Click the changed account again. Its changes are listed on top: what changed, the kind, the story, who made it and when, and its effect on the NOI.

marks.label: The change
marks.text: With its story and its effect on the NOI.

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens it with its figures, to change.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes it out (asks first).

steps.text: Click **Edit** to change its figures or its story, then **Save the edit**. Or click **Remove** to take it out; the app asks first.

callouts.text: The underwriting’s **History** keeps every change, edit and removal, with its story.

sections.title: Credit all revenue at once
sections.text: When the property runs better now than the year shows — it filled up, or rents went up — annualize every revenue account at once from its last months.

steps.text: Close the window and click **Revenue credit…** in the underwriting bar.
Click **T3 — last 3 months**, or T6, or T12. Each revenue account becomes its last 3 months × 4 (or 6 × 2).
Write the story and click **Save the revenue credit**.

marks.label: T3 / T6 / T12
marks.text: How many recent months.

marks.label: Annualized
marks.text: Each revenue line after the credit.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: Required.

marks.label: Save the revenue credit
marks.text: Saves it.

callouts.text: The management fee doesn’t follow the revenue credit. Aggressive uses Safe’s credit until you give it its own.

Let Claude find the changes a lender would accept.

pages.title: Add an account
pages.description: Add income or a cost the T12 has no account for, with its amount and its story.
pages.intro: Some money isn’t in the T12 at all: an antenna lease signed after its year, a PILOT tax, bad debt at a market norm. Add it as an account of its own, under the line it belongs to, with its amount, its kind and its story.
before: A T12 for the property — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: Click **+ Add an account** in the underwriting bar. A window lists every line by section: the ones in your T12 first, then the ones it doesn’t have.

marks.label: A line the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: Adding an account here adds the line to the underwriting.

steps.text: Click the line the money belongs to. Here **Antenna Income**.
Type the **Account name**, as the lender will see it.
Click **Its amount** and type a year’s figure. Or click **Per unit** for dollars per apartment a year (on an expense line, **% of revenue** is there too).
Pick the **Kind**, choose where it applies under **Apply to**, and write the **Story**.

marks.label: Account name
marks.text: What the lender will see.

marks.label: Its amount
marks.text: A year’s figure.

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Here only in Aggressive.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Nothing in Safe; $500 a month in Aggressive.

steps.text: Click **Save the change**.

next.text: Change an account the T12 already has.
Approve Safe and Aggressive when they’re ready.

pages.title: Use Claude’s stories and suggestions
pages.description: Let Claude find the accounts a lender would accept changing, and put the ones you agree with into the draft.
pages.intro: Claude reads every account month by month and suggests changes a lender would accept, each with its story — only ones that raise the NOI, and only ones it confirmed. Your own assumptions suggest changes too, when a line runs worse than them. Nothing goes into the draft until you open the account, check it and save it.

callouts.text: Claude works from four sources, and only four: the T12 (the source of truth), the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details (its units and address). It searches the web only for the surroundings, such as the weather around the property in a given month. Where it has to assume, it says so under **Checked**.

before: A T12 for the property — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: Click **Claude’s stories…** in the underwriting bar. The page scrolls to Claude’s stories under the table, and the first time, Claude starts reading. It can take a few minutes.
Read the stories. Each card has the account and its change, the story, how Claude got the number, what to show the lender, and what Claude checked.

marks.label: A story
marks.text: One account, its change and its story, and how much it raises the NOI.

marks.label: How Claude got the number
marks.text: From the T12’s own figures.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this.

marks.label: Claude didn’t have
marks.text: Shows only when one of the four sources is missing.

callouts.text: A story Claude couldn’t confirm is never shown, and one that would lower the NOI is listed as left out. When the “Claude didn’t have” note names a missing source, add it and click **Look again**.

sections.title: Put a story in the draft

steps.text: On a story you agree with, click **Put it in the draft**. The account opens in the pro forma window, with the change and its story filled in.

marks.label: Claude suggests

marks.label: Its new amount

sections.title: Use a suggestion from your assumptions
sections.text: When a line runs worse than your assumption, its biggest account gets a suggestion at the assumption, with a ready story. Here the management fee runs 3% of revenue against an assumption of 2.5%.

steps.text: Click the yellow **suggestions** button in the underwriting bar. It lists every open suggestion, from your assumptions and from Claude.

marks.label: A suggestion

marks.label: Open the account

marks.label: The suggestion

marks.label: Not this one

marks.label: Kind

pages.title: Approve the underwriting
pages.description: Make Safe and Aggressive the property’s underwriting, so the refinance, the roll-up and What to push use them.
pages.intro: Until you approve it, the underwriting is a draft that nothing else uses. Approving makes Safe and Aggressive the property’s underwriting: the refinance, the portfolio roll-up and What to push work from them. You can change the draft later and approve it again.

Pick **Safe only**, or **Safe and Aggressive** side by side.

marks.text: One version.

marks.label: Safe and Aggressive

pages.title: See what you can still push
pages.description: Read Claude’s list of what can still raise the NOI after the approved underwriting, measured on each version.
pages.intro: The approved underwriting holds what a lender accepts today. What to push is what you can still do from there to raise the NOI — raise rents at renewal, re-bid a contract, cut a cost that runs above its benchmark — measured on the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive. It’s your plan, not the lender’s.
before: The underwriting approved — see [Approve the underwriting](approve-the-underwriting).

steps.text: Scroll to **What to push on this property**, at the bottom of the tab. Claude starts by itself once the underwriting is approved, and again each time you approve it. It can take a few minutes.
Read each push: what to do and why, its effect three ways, the lever it pulls, and what Claude checked.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: What to do, and why, from this property’s own figures.

marks.label: Its effect, three ways
marks.text: On the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive.

marks.label: The lever
marks.text: What it pulls.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this.

callouts.text: The figures are Claude’s estimates: a starting point, not advice.

steps.text: Click **Re-analyse** to ask Claude again — after you add the rent roll or the loan agreement, for example.
To see what loan the pushes would get you, tick them in the refinance. See [Plan what to push for a refinance](plan-what-to-push).

sections.title: How Claude chooses
sections.text: Claude works from four sources, and only four: the T12 (the source of truth), the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details (units, address). It searches the web for the surroundings: market rents and rent growth, or the weather or an event in a given month. Every push raises the NOI on every version, never pulls a lever a story in the underwriting already pulls, and lists what Claude checked; one it couldn’t confirm is never shown. The “Claude didn’t have” note shows only when one of the four sources is missing.

callouts.text: Claude works out who pays the utilities from the T12 itself. A utilities line big enough for the whole property means the owner pays, in the rent, so Claude never suggests billing the residents for them. A line only big enough for the common areas means the residents pay their own.
Some vacancy is natural, so there is no push toward 100% occupancy. Rent growth at the market’s usual rate is measured on top of the rent the underwriting already counts.

next.text: Tick the pushes in the refinance.
See the largest loan each version supports.
Every part of a push, named.

pages.title: Size the debt
pages.description: See the largest loan Safe and Aggressive each support, at the limits you set for the property.
pages.intro: Debt sizing is a quick answer while you underwrite: the largest loan each version of the underwriting supports, at your cap rate, LTV, coverage and debt-yield limits. The refinance sizes the real loan with its lender’s own limits.
before: A T12 for the property — see [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: Scroll to **Debt sizing**, under the underwriting table.
Type the property’s limits: **Cap rate**, **Max LTV**, **Min DSCR** and **Min debt yield**, and the **Interest rate** and **Amortization** the payment is worked out at.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Max LTV
marks.text: The loan as a share of that value.

marks.label: Min DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly payment must be at least this.

marks.label: Min debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ the loan must be at least this.

steps.text: Read **Max supportable** for Safe and for Aggressive: the smallest of the loans the limits allow. **Binds on** names the limit that sets it.

marks.label: Max supportable — Safe
marks.text: On the Safe underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Max supportable — Aggressive
marks.text: On the Aggressive underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Binds on
marks.text: The limit that sets it.

marks.label: Implied
marks.text: The LTV, DSCR and debt yield at that loan.

callouts.text: Debt sizing works on the underwriting as it stands, draft or approved.

Every figure in Debt sizing, named.

pages.title: The Underwriting tab
pages.description: Every part of the Underwriting & Sizing tab, from the property’s T12 at the top to What to push at the bottom.
pages.intro: The tab works top to bottom: the property and its T12, the figures it gives, the underwriting table with its bar, Claude’s stories and your assumptions, debt sizing, the property’s operating history, the portfolio roll-up and What to push. The pictures show a made-up property with its underwriting approved. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

marks.text: This tab.

marks.label: Revenue credit…
marks.text: Annualizes every revenue account at once from its last months.

marks.label: + Add an account
marks.text: An account the T12 doesn’t have.

marks.label: For the lender…
marks.text: The Excel file for the lender.

marks.label: History
marks.text: Every change with its story, and every approval.

marks.label: Start over
marks.text: Takes every change out and starts again from the T12 (asks first). The history keeps them, and the last approval stays in use until you approve again.

marks.label: Approved by …
marks.text: Who approved it, when, and the Safe and Aggressive NOI the refinance, the roll-up and What to push use.

views.title: A warning from an assumption
views.text: An assumption that would lower the NOI is never a suggestion. Here the management fee assumption is set to 4%, but the T12 runs 3%: the bar warns you, for your information, and the underwriting keeps the T12’s figure. To underwrite 4% anyway, change the account yourself, with its story.

marks.label: The warning
marks.text: Your assumption, what the T12 runs, and how much lower the NOI would be at your assumption.

marks.label: The NOIs
marks.text: Unchanged: an assumption never moves the underwriting by itself.

views.title: History
views.text: Opened by **History**: every change, edit, removal and set-aside, newest first — which line and account, old → new, the kind and story, who and when. Each approval is kept here too.

marks.label: An entry
marks.text: One change, with its story.
Closes the history.

views.title: The columns
views.text: Every line of the T12, classified. Two figures per line, each also per unit: the T12 and the underwriting.

marks.label: Line
marks.text: The underwriting line. A line far from its benchmark is flagged next to its name.

marks.label: In-Place (T12)
marks.text: Each line as the statement shows it.

marks.label: $/unit
marks.text: The figure ÷ the units.

marks.label: Underwriting · Safe
marks.text: The underwriting, line by line, in the version the switch shows.

marks.label: A figure
marks.text: Click it: the line’s accounts open in the pro forma window. See [The pro forma window](ref-pro-forma).

marks.label: Teal dot
marks.text: The line has changes (here the revenue credit). Hover its figure to see their kinds.

marks.label: Yellow dot
marks.text: Suggestions wait on this line.

views.title: The reserves and the NOI
views.text: Subtotals for rental income, effective gross income and expenses, then the replacement reserves and the Net Operating Income, each in both columns and per unit.

marks.label: Effective Gross Income
marks.text: All income after vacancy and the other deductions.

marks.label: Total Operating Expenses
marks.text: Every expense line added up.

marks.label: Replacement reserves
marks.text: Your reserves per unit × the units: a line in Safe and Aggressive (the T12 has none).

marks.label: Net Operating Income
marks.text: The in-place NOI and the underwriting NOI, each per unit.

marks.label: Underwriting NOI
marks.text: After the reserves, in the version the switch shows.

views.text: Under the table, one box per version, checked to the dollar: the T12 NOI, every change grouped by its kind with its story, the NOI before reserves, the replacement reserves and the underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Safe — how it adds up
marks.text: T12 NOI + each change − reserves = the Safe underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Aggressive — how it adds up
marks.text: The same for Aggressive.

marks.label: reconciles to the dollar
marks.text: The changes add up exactly (worked out twice).

marks.label: Revenue credit
marks.text: A group: every change of one kind, each with its story.

marks.label: − Replacement reserves
marks.text: Your reserves per unit × the units, taken off both versions.

marks.label: = Safe underwriting NOI
marks.text: The figure that is approved, sized and refinanced on.

sections.title: Claude’s stories
sections.text: Under the table. Claude reads the T12 account by account, month by month, with the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details, and searches the web around the property. It offers stories a lender would accept: only ones that raise the NOI, and only ones it confirmed. Nothing goes in until you open the account and save it. See [Use Claude’s stories and suggestions](use-claudes-stories).

marks.label: Look again
marks.text: Asks Claude again (**Find stories with Claude** the first time). Needs Claude connected.

marks.label: A story
marks.text: One account, one change, its kind and story, and how much it raises the NOI.

marks.label: How Claude got the number
marks.text: From the statement’s own figures.

marks.label: To back it with the lender
marks.text: What you show the lender to prove it.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this: the T12’s months, the rent roll, the loan agreement, the property details, or a web page with its site and date. A story it couldn’t confirm is never shown.

marks.label: Claude didn’t have
marks.text: Shows only when one of Claude’s four sources is missing: the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement or the property details (units, address). Claude worked from what it had; add the missing one and click **Look again**.

marks.label: The web
marks.text: How many times Claude searched the web for this, and what it searched.

marks.label: Put it in the draft
marks.text: Opens the account with the story filled in, to check and save.

marks.label: In the pro forma ✓
marks.text: Already in the draft.

views.text: Under Claude’s stories, per property. They don’t change the underwriting by themselves: a line that runs worse than an assumption gets a suggestion in the draft (never one that lowers the NOI), and the reserves per unit are taken off Safe and Aggressive. Each change is kept in the property’s history.

marks.label: Vacancy
marks.text: When the T12 runs above it, the vacancy account gets a suggestion at it; when the T12 already runs below it, a warning. Never applied by itself.

marks.label: Management fee
marks.text: As a % of effective gross income: a suggestion when the T12 runs above it, a warning when it would lower the NOI.

marks.label: Reserves / unit
marks.text: Replacement reserves a year per unit, taken off Safe and Aggressive.

marks.label: Payroll / unit
marks.text: Your payroll benchmark for this property. A payroll line 15% off it is flagged.

marks.label: R&M / unit
marks.text: Your repairs and maintenance benchmark.

marks.label: Save to property record
marks.text: Saves the assumptions and benchmarks with the property, so every screen uses them.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to these, old → new, who and when.

views.text: The largest loan each version supports, side by side, at the limits you set for this property. Each limit gives a loan on each version’s NOI; the smallest is the maximum supportable loan. See [Size the debt](size-the-debt).

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Max LTV
marks.text: The loan as a share of that value.

marks.label: Min DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ the yearly payment must be at least this.

marks.label: Min debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ the loan must be at least this.

marks.label: Interest rate
marks.text: The rate the payment is worked out at.

marks.label: Amortization
marks.text: The years the payment pays the loan down over.

marks.label: Safe
marks.text: Sized on the Safe underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Sized on the Aggressive underwriting NOI.

marks.label: Est. value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Loan @ LTV
marks.text: What the LTV limit allows.

marks.label: Loan @ DSCR
marks.text: What the coverage limit allows.

marks.label: Loan @ debt yield
marks.text: What the debt-yield limit allows.

marks.label: Max supportable — Safe
marks.text: The smallest of the three.

marks.label: Max supportable — Aggressive
marks.text: The same on Aggressive.

marks.label: Binds on
marks.text: The limit that sets it.

marks.label: Implied LTV · DSCR · debt yield
marks.text: The ratios at the maximum loan.

views.text: The General Data card. Every T12 you upload adds its months (up to 24 are kept). The card shows the in-place NOI and the approved underwriting (Safe · Aggressive); each line shows its trailing 12 months and the change against the 12 before. Click its title to fold it; the app remembers.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: The same NOI as everywhere in the app, and how it was worked out.

marks.label: Underwriting NOI — Safe · Aggressive
marks.text: The approved underwriting, and when it was approved (“not approved yet” before).

marks.label: Saved to the folder
marks.text: Kept in the property’s folder (general-data.json).

marks.label: Trailing 12-mo
marks.text: Each line’s last 12 months, and its change.

marks.label: Fold
marks.text: Click the title to fold the card or open it again.

views.text: Every property: units, loans, in-place NOI, the approved Safe and Aggressive underwriting NOI (blank until approved), balance, yearly debt service, DSCR, debt yield, LTV and maturity, with a total row.

marks.label: In-place NOI
marks.text: Each property’s NOI.

marks.label: Safe UW NOI
marks.text: The approved Safe underwriting; blank until it is approved.

marks.label: Aggressive UW NOI
marks.text: The approved Aggressive underwriting, beside Safe.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ its yearly debt service.

marks.label: A property
marks.text: Click it to open it here.

sections.title: What to push
sections.text: At the bottom of the tab. It runs by itself once the underwriting is approved, and again when you approve again; before that it reads “Approve the underwriting first”. Claude reads the same four sources as for the stories — the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement and the property details — with the approved underwriting, and searches the web around the property. These pushes are your plan, not the lender’s. See [See what you can still push](use-what-to-push).

marks.label: Re-analyse
marks.text: Asks Claude again.

marks.label: A push
marks.text: What to do, why (from this property’s own figures) and the effort.

marks.label: Its effect, three ways
marks.text: On the in-place T12, on Safe and on Aggressive, each net of what that version already counts. Claude’s estimates: a starting point, not advice.

marks.label: The lever
marks.text: What it pulls: never one a story in the underwriting already pulls.

marks.label: Beside the story
marks.text: The underwriting story it sits next to: a different lever, so both count.

marks.label: Checked
marks.text: What Claude checked before it suggested this push. One it couldn’t confirm is never shown.

marks.label: Claude didn’t have
marks.text: Shows only when one of the four sources is missing: the T12, the rent roll, the loan agreement or the property details. Claude worked from what it had; add the missing one and click **Re-analyse**.

marks.label: The web
marks.text: How many times Claude searched the web for this, and what it searched.

callouts.text: Claude works out who pays the utilities from the T12: a utilities line big enough for the whole property means the owner pays, in the rent, so no billing them back; one only big enough for the common areas means the residents pay their own. There is no push toward 100% occupancy, and next year’s rent growth at the market’s usual rate is measured on top of the underwritten rent.

pages.title: The pro forma window
pages.description: The window that opens over the Underwriting tab: a line’s accounts, every way to change one, the suggestions, and the windows for a new account, the revenue credit and the lender file.
pages.intro: Click a figure in the Underwriting column, or a tool in the underwriting bar, and this window opens over the tab, about 80% of the screen. Nothing in it is saved until you click its save button. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: Opened by a figure in the **Underwriting** column. On top, the line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive. Below, every account of the line — none hidden, a $0 one too — with its 12 months as the statement shows them.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: The whole line in the T12, in Safe and in Aggressive, each per unit.

marks.label: An account
marks.text: Its row in the file, its 12 months, its T12, Safe and Aggressive. Click it to change it.

marks.label: T12
marks.text: The account’s year in the statement.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive
marks.text: The account in each version; a changed one in bold.

marks.label: A change’s tag
marks.text: Where the change applies and its kind. Hover it to read the story.

marks.label: A $0 account
marks.text: Shown with its twelve zeros: nothing is hidden.

marks.label: The line
marks.text: Each month and each column added up.

marks.label: + Add an account the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: For money the statement has no account for.
Closes the window.

sections.title: Ways to change an account
sections.text: Click an account and its choices open right under it. Each change has a kind, the versions it applies to and a story. See [Change an account](change-an-account).

views.title: The choices
views.text: Which ways show depends on the account: **% of revenue**, for one, only on an expense or a rent deduction.

marks.label: New amount
marks.text: Type the account’s new yearly figure. Type 0 to take it out: the lender’s file then reads “Took out”.

marks.label: Spread over years
marks.text: A cost paid once every few years counts only its share for one year.

marks.label: Annualize
marks.text: The account becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months.

marks.label: % of revenue
marks.text: The account as a % of revenue (expenses and rental deductions).

marks.label: Per unit
marks.text: A dollar figure per apartment a year × the units.

views.title: New amount, kind and story
views.text: Here the snow-removal change, opened again with **Edit**. The preview shows the account’s 12 months before and after, the line and the NOI.

marks.label: Its new amount
marks.text: The yearly figure for this account.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Why it changes: non-recurring, spread over years, normalized, operating change, market norm or partnership/back-office (and revenue credit when you annualize income).

marks.label: Apply to
marks.text: Safe, Aggressive or Both.

marks.label: Same story as…
marks.text: The stories already in this underwriting, with their account. Pick one and it fills in.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads. Required.

marks.label: Draft it with Claude
marks.text: Claude writes a first draft from the account’s months; you edit it.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: The account’s 12 months in the T12 and after the change (each month in proportion).

marks.label: ready to save
marks.text: Or what is still missing.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: **Save the change**, or **Save the edit** for one you opened with Edit. The window stays open on the line.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the choices without saving.

views.title: Spread over years
views.text: For a cost paid once every few years that landed in this T12. Exterior painting cost $14,400 in May and is done every 5 years: the underwriting counts $14,400 ÷ 5 = $2,880 a year. It divides the whole account; for an account that mixes normal monthly costs with one big bill, use **New amount** instead.

marks.label: Paid every … years
marks.text: How often it is paid; it counts one share a year.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Set to “Spread over years” by itself.

marks.label: Before → after
marks.text: $14,400 in May becomes $2,880 for the year.

views.title: Annualize
views.text: When an account runs differently in its recent months — a new contract, a rent increase — it becomes its last 3, 6 or 12 months × 12 ÷ the months. Each choice shows what it gives. On a normal 12-month T12 the last 12 months are the T12 itself, so that choice is greyed (“same as the T12”).

marks.label: Last 3 months
marks.text: × 4: here $28,400 a year.

marks.label: Last 12 months
marks.text: Only different from the T12 when the file has more than 12 months, or the T12 rule used the last 3 months × 4.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: The months it comes from.

marks.label: Kind
marks.text: Operating change for an expense; Revenue credit for an income account.

views.title: % of revenue
views.text: An expense as a % of that version’s effective gross income, or a rent deduction (vacancy, bad debt) as a % of gross potential rent. Because you chose it, it moves when that version’s revenue moves. The management fee never moves by itself.

marks.text: The percentage.

marks.label: It follows revenue
marks.text: Only because you picked % of revenue.

marks.label: The management fee
marks.text: Stays at the T12 unless you change its account.

views.title: Per unit
views.text: A dollar figure per apartment a year, times the units (120 here): for a cost quoted per unit, such as a maintenance role or turnover.

marks.label: $ per unit a year
marks.text: × the property’s units.

marks.label: Aggressive
marks.text: Here only in the Aggressive version.

marks.label: Preview
marks.text: Safe unchanged; Aggressive $300 × 120 = $36,000.

views.title: A suggestion on an account
views.text: When a line runs worse than your assumption, its biggest account gets a suggestion at the assumption, with a ready story, and a **Suggested** chip in its row (**Claude suggests** for one of Claude’s stories). Here the management fee runs 3% of revenue against an assumption of 2.5%. A suggestion only ever raises the NOI, and nothing is applied by itself.

marks.label: Suggested
marks.text: A suggestion waits on this account.

marks.label: The suggestion
marks.text: The change, its kind, the ready story and why.

marks.label: Use this
marks.text: Fills the change and its story in; you can still edit them before you save.

marks.label: Not this one
marks.text: Sets it aside (**Bring it back** undoes it).

views.title: Every suggestion in one list
views.text: Opened by the yellow **suggestions** button in the underwriting bar: every open suggestion, from your assumptions and from Claude.

marks.label: A suggestion
marks.text: Where, what and its story.

marks.label: Open the account
marks.text: Opens the line with the suggestion filled in.

views.text: Opened by **+ Add an account** in the underwriting bar: every line by section — rental income and deductions, other income, expenses — the ones in your T12 first. Pick the line, then name the account and fill it in like any other change. See [Add an account](add-an-account).

marks.label: A line in the underwriting
marks.text: The new account goes under it.

marks.label: A line the T12 doesn’t have
marks.text: Marked “(not in the T12)”: an account here adds the line to the underwriting.

views.text: Opened by **Revenue credit…** in the underwriting bar: every revenue account annualized at once from its last months, for when the property runs better now than the year shows. The table shows each revenue line month by month, the months used highlighted, the T12 and the annualized figure; with a rent roll, today’s occupancy too. A story is required. The management fee doesn’t follow it.

marks.label: Safe / Aggressive (its own)
marks.text: Aggressive can have its own; until then it uses Safe’s.

marks.label: T3 / T6 / T12
marks.text: How many recent months. T12 changes nothing on a normal 12-month file.

marks.label: Months used
marks.text: Which months.

marks.label: Annualized
marks.text: Each line after the credit.

marks.label: Story
marks.text: The reason the lender reads.

marks.label: Save the revenue credit
marks.text: Saves it.

views.text: Opened by **For the lender…** in the underwriting bar: an Excel file with four sheets — **Pro forma** (each line with its change, kind and story, and the reserves), **Changed accounts**, **Reconciliation** and **Monthly** (the months used for the revenue credit marked). See [Approve the underwriting](approve-the-underwriting#give-the-lender-the-file).

marks.label: Safe only
marks.text: One version.

marks.label: Safe and Aggressive
marks.text: Both, side by side.

marks.label: Save the Excel file…
marks.text: Asks where to save “<property> — Pro forma — <date>.xlsx”.
